# Harden the automatically generated local Root Key File

An automatically generated Local Root Key File lives in a dedicated platform security directory outside Positron data, temporary, and backup roots. User installations use the platform configuration directory, system packages use an administrator-owned secrets directory, and containers should mount it as a separate persistent secret volume. Positron creates the directory and file with owner-only access using exclusive no-follow operations, durably synchronizes the file and parent, and on every startup verifies that it is a regular single-link file with expected ownership, permissions, version, and fingerprint. Symbolic links, hard links, unsafe permissions, unexpected ownership, and filesystems unable to enforce these controls are rejected with no insecure override. The versioned file contains local-provider identity, key ID, creation metadata, integrity checksum, and the 256-bit Root KEK because encrypting it would require another root secret. Startup warnings state that local filesystem custody does not protect against compromise or theft of both key and data.
